image_description: A close-up, vertical shot of a grey whale's head and rostrum emerging vertically from deep blue water. The whale's snout is pointed upwards, displaying the characteristic arched rostrum and two blowholes at the apex. The skin is dark grey/black with significant white mottling and patches indicative of barnacles and cyamids. Water splashes around the base of the emergence. No dorsal fin or tail flukes are visible due to the framing.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly shows the arched rostrum and the twin blowhole structure at the top of the head, consistent with grey whale anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture exhibits high-contrast white speckling and patches against a dark background, accurately representing barnacle/cyamid colonization.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is cropped tightly on the head/rostrum; the posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be located is completely outside the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the anterior head section is visible; the full body shape cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible skin on the head confirms the mottled pattern described in the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or obscured by the angle and water splash; internal baleen structures are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further back on the body and are not visible in this head-only crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail flukes are at the posterior end and are completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The surface of the rostrum shows irregular, rough textures consistent with callosities and barnacle clusters.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The water splash around the whale's head has a slightly 'smudged' or painterly quality rather than crisp droplet definition, typical of AI generation struggling with fluid dynamics, but not structurally breaking.
The very tip of the rostrum appears slightly softened and lacks the sharp geometric definition expected in a high-resolution photograph, possibly due to generative blur.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that the subject is indeed a grey whale and not another cetacean species (e.g., humpback or right whale) based on head shape and skin pattern.
To critically assess the realism of the water splash and the boundary between the whale's skin and the water, checking for melting or blending artifacts.
To ensure the whale's head is a single coherent object without floating fragments or disconnected skin patches, especially given the complex mottling.

focus_areas: Verification of rostrum arch and blowhole placement
Water splash physics and boundary sharpness
Absence of dorsal fin artifacts in the visible area
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the texture of the white patches on the whale's head. In real grey whales, these are barnacles and whale lice which have specific 3D relief. AI often renders these as flat white paint splatters. Check if the perceptual quality auditor detects a lack of depth in these patches. Also, verify if the water line interacts correctly with the skin or if there is 'bleeding' where the grey skin merges into the blue water unnaturally.
